Mark Beach graduated from the University of York (U.K.) in 1983 with a first class B.Sc honours degree in Electronic Engineering. After an initial period with the GEC Hirst Research Laboratories, he joined the Department of Electrical & Electronic Engineering at the University of Bristol as a postgraduate student. Dr Beach then received his Ph.D. in 1989 for his work on adaptive antennas for multiple spread spectrum signal sources, primarily targeted towards GPS receiver technology. Postdoctoral research at Bristol included work regarding the application of adaptive antenna techniques to mobile cellular networks for which the research team received the IEEE Neal Shepherd memorial prize in 1990 for the best Antenna and Propagation paper published in the Vehicular Technology Proceedings in 1990. Since August 1990, Dr Beach has been engaged as a member of lecturing staff at Bristol and heads the CDMA and wideband propagation research acivities within the Centre for Communications Research. Here, Dr Beach has led a range of activities in the field of mobile radio, including the joint development of an integrated Inmarsat-C and GPS receiver. Currently, Dr Beach holds the U.K. DTI/EPSRC LINK grant concerning the evaluation of CDMA techniques for UMTS, and is also the project manager of the EC RACEII TSUNAMI (R2108) project concerning the application of adaptive antenna technology to 3rd generation wireless networks.
